content:
Alex: heads up — starting a thread for a concrete proposal on admission-control for Dedicated surge fairness. idea: implement a soft admission layer that enforces sustained throughput caps + short-term burst credits per tenant. want quick feedback before i turn this into a spec.

Maya: love the approach. we need a clear fairness metric (not just tokens). suggest using 5-min EWMA of tokens/sec and a normalized fairness ratio per tenant.

Sam: +1. also add a degradation budget so high-paying customers can opt into guaranteed minimal latency during spikes. call it `grace_budget` and measured in vGPU-seconds.

Jin: curious about enforcement. are we talking hard preempts or throttling with HTTP 429? my vote: throttling + progressive quality degrade (lower seq_len or quantized model) before 429.

Alex: agree. sequence: 1) soft-admit until sustained cap, 2) if exceeded kick in `spill_policy` (throttle -> degrade -> preempt). default is throttle then degrade. fallback policy per tenant.

Maya: operationally we need observable signals: `admit_rate`, `spill_rate`, `degrade_count`, `latency_p99_by_tenant`. add to Redwood Console as per-route charts.

Sam: for predictive admission, we could use a 1-min predictive EWMA of queue length and apply a small guardband for autoscale lag. saves surprise.

Jin: can we sketch a tiny config for tenant-level policy? quick proto: 
```json
{"tenant_id":"acme","sustained_cap_rps":"200","burst_credits":5000,"grace_budget":3000,"spill_policy":"throttle,degrade,preempt"}
```

Alex: that matches what i had in mind. launch criteria (proposed):
- policy can be toggled per-tenant (opt-in)
- metrics available in Console and alertable
- regression test: under synthetic 3x surge, p95 latency for opted-in tenants < 2x baseline, fairness_ratio within 10% across tenants
- integration tests for fallback to hosted-compatible model variants

Maya: add a customer acceptance checklist: Mapbox pilot + one fintech pilot (needs HSM/compliance check). both to validate billing and SLA claims.

Sam: rollout plan idea: feature-flag -> beta tenants -> 2-week pilot with observability -> adjust parameters -> wider GA. also require migration doc for existing reserved pools.

Jin: ops-bot note: runbook hooks required. oncall should be able to: 1) flip tenant to `best_effort`, 2) drain burst credits, 3) forcibly preempt.

ops-bot: created runbook stub: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-admit. (auto)

Alex: risks/unknowns: accurate tenant accounting at high TPS, cross-region fairness when tenants span regions, cost implications of degradation paths. need SRE and infra input on metering and metastore latency.

Maya: prioritize infra work: per-tenant counters must be <5ms read/write on hot path. if not, we'll need approximate counters (Sketch/HyperLogLog) and softer SLAs.

Sam: next steps: Alex to draft RFC with config schema + rollout checklist, Jin to own runbook additions, Maya to scope Console charts, Ops to pick two beta tenants. target RFC in 1 week. :thumbsup:

Alex: thanks — i’ll post RFC draft tomorrow. ping me @Sam @Maya if you want early review.
